question: How does adjustment for mature host-transcript length affect the association between host-transcript RBP burden and ncORF ribosome occupancy?
status: Post hoc sensitivity analysis; not preregistered.
population: Original S2 main catalogue, amino-acid length <=100, and each cell's own TPM>=1 and complete original model inputs. Do not use a both-cell intersection or the clustering subset.
exposure: log1p(distinct RBPs detected across host-transcript exons), original all-assayed panel per cell
length: Mature spliced transcript length in nucleotides. Recompute from the GENCODE v35 transcript FASTA and require exact agreement with prior exon-union length for every main host ENST. Never substitute genomic span.
additional_sensitivities: Original model + cubic B-spline of log(mature transcript length), df=4, include_intercept=False
Original model + log(mature transcript length) + fixed effects for five transcript-length quantile groups
Original model + log(mature transcript length) + categorical ORF biotype
Original model + log(mature transcript length), restricted to transcripts carrying exactly one analysed ORF in the per-cell model population
Original model + log(mature transcript length), fitted separately in the five length groups
length_groups: Per-cell quintile boundaries calculated on unique host transcripts, not duplicated ORF rows; all ORFs on one transcript share a group.
inference: OLS point estimates; CR1 transcript and stable-ENSG gene-clustered standard errors, finite-sample corrections and t intervals with cluster-count minus one degrees of freedom. 95% intervals are pointwise sensitivity summaries, not selection-adjusted confirmation.
report: incremental R-squared from adding the RBP term to otherwise identical covariates
length-versus-binding Spearman correlation on unique hosts
all model results without result-dependent selection
limits: Adjustment tests dependence on measured transcript length under specified models; it does not remove all unmeasured confounding, recover biological replication, or establish causation or ORF-selective regulation.
